items.name: Precedence
items.summary: Operators for which precedence must be defined.

items.name: dialect_from_str
items.signature: fn dialect_from_str(dialect_name: impl AsRef<str>) -> Option<Box<dyn Dialect>>
items.summary: Returns the built in [`Dialect`] corresponding to `dialect_name`.

items.name: Dialect
items.summary: Encapsulates the differences between SQL implementations.

methods.name: allow_extract_custom
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect allows the `EXTRACT` function to words other than [`Keyword`].

methods.name: allow_extract_single_quotes
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect allows the `EXTRACT` function to use single quotes in the part being extracted.

methods.name: convert_type_before_value
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect has a CONVERT function which accepts a type first and an expression second, e.g. `CONVERT(varchar, 1)`

methods.name: describe_requires_table_keyword
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect requires the `TABLE` keyword after `DESCRIBE`

methods.name: dialect
methods.summary: Determine the [`TypeId`] of this dialect.

methods.name: get_next_precedence
methods.summary: Dialect-specific precedence override

methods.name: get_next_precedence_default
methods.summary: Get the precedence of the next token, looking at the full token stream.

methods.name: get_reserved_grantees_types
methods.summary: Returns grantee types that should be treated as identifiers

methods.name: get_reserved_keywords_for_select_item_operator
methods.summary: Returns reserved keywords that may prefix a select item expression e.g. `SELECT CONNECT_BY_ROOT name FROM Tbl2` (Snowflake)

methods.name: identifier_quote_style
methods.summary: Return the character used to quote identifiers.

methods.name: ignores_wildcard_escapes
methods.summary: Determine whether the dialect strips the backslash when escaping LIKE wildcards (%, _).

methods.name: is_column_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword should be parsed as a column identifier. See [keywords::RESERVED_FOR_COLUMN_ALIAS]

methods.name: is_custom_operator_part
methods.summary: Most dialects do not have custom operators. Override this method to provide custom operators.

methods.name: is_delimited_identifier_start
methods.summary: Determine if a character starts a quoted identifier. The default implementation, accepting "double quoted" ids is both ANSI-compliant and appropriate for most dialects (with the notable exception of MySQL, MS SQL, and sqlite). You can acce…

methods.name: is_identifier_generating_function_name
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect considers the specified ident as a function that returns an identifier. Typically used to generate identifiers programmatically.

methods.name: is_identifier_part
methods.summary: Determine if a character is a valid unquoted identifier character

methods.name: is_identifier_start
methods.summary: Determine if a character is a valid start character for an unquoted identifier

methods.name: is_nested_delimited_identifier_start
methods.summary: Determine if a character starts a potential nested quoted identifier. Example: RedShift supports the following quote styles to all mean the same thing: ```sql SELECT 1 AS foo; SELECT 1 AS "foo"; SELECT 1 AS [foo]; SELECT 1 AS ["foo"]; ```

methods.name: is_reserved_for_identifier
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword is reserved and cannot be used as an identifier without special handling like quoting.

methods.name: is_select_item_alias
methods.signature: fn is_select_item_alias(&self, explicit: bool, kw: &Keyword, parser: &mut Parser<'_>) -> bool
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword should be parsed as a select item alias. When explicit is true, the keyword is preceded by an `AS` word. Parser is provided to enable looking ahead if needed.

methods.name: is_table_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword should be parsed as a table factor alias. See [keywords::RESERVED_FOR_TABLE_ALIAS]

methods.name: is_table_factor
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword should be parsed as a table factor identifier. See [keywords::RESERVED_FOR_TABLE_FACTOR]

methods.name: is_table_factor_alias
methods.signature: fn is_table_factor_alias(&self, explicit: bool, kw: &Keyword, parser: &mut Parser<'_>) -> bool
methods.summary: Returns true if the specified keyword should be parsed as a table factor alias. When explicit is true, the keyword is preceded by an `AS` word. Parser is provided to enable looking ahead if needed.

methods.name: parse_column_option
methods.summary: Dialect-specific column option parser override

methods.name: parse_infix
methods.signature: fn parse_infix(&self, _parser: &mut Parser<'_>, _expr: &Expr, _precedence: u8) -> Option<Result<Expr, ParserError>>
methods.summary: Dialect-specific infix parser override

methods.name: parse_prefix
methods.summary: Dialect-specific prefix parser override

methods.name: parse_statement
methods.summary: Dialect-specific statement parser override

methods.name: peek_nested_delimited_identifier_quotes
methods.summary: Only applicable whenever [`Self::is_nested_delimited_identifier_start`] returns true If the next sequence of tokens potentially represent a nested identifier, then this method returns a tuple containing the outer quote style, and if presen…

methods.name: prec_unknown
methods.summary: Returns the precedence when the precedence is otherwise unknown

methods.name: prec_value
methods.summary: Decide the lexical Precedence of operators.

methods.name: require_interval_qualifier
methods.summary: Whether `INTERVAL` expressions require units (called "qualifiers" in the ANSI SQL spec) to be specified, e.g. `INTERVAL 1 DAY` vs `INTERVAL 1`.

methods.name: requires_single_line_comment_whitespace
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect requires a whitespace character after `--` to start a single line comment.

methods.name: support_map_literal_syntax
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports defining object using the syntax like `Map {1: 10, 2: 20}`.

methods.name: supports_alter_column_type_using
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `USING` clause in an `ALTER COLUMN` statement. Example:  ```sql  ALTER TABLE tbl ALTER COLUMN col SET DATA TYPE <type> USING <exp>` ```

methods.name: supports_array_join_syntax
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports ClickHouse-style `ARRAY JOIN` / `LEFT ARRAY JOIN` / `INNER ARRAY JOIN` syntax for unnesting arrays inline.

methods.name: supports_array_typedef_with_brackets
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports array type definition with brackets with an optional size. For example: ```CREATE TABLE my_table (arr1 INT[], arr2 INT[3])``` ```SELECT x::INT[]```

methods.name: supports_array_typedef_without_element_type
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `ARRAY` type without specifying an element type.

methods.name: supports_asc_desc_in_column_definition
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `ASC` and `DESC` in column definitions e.g. `CREATE TABLE t (a INT ASC, b INT DESC);`

methods.name: supports_bang_not_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `!a` syntax for boolean `NOT` expressions.

methods.name: supports_binary_kw_as_cast
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports casting an expression to a binary type using the `BINARY <expr>` syntax.

methods.name: supports_bitwise_shift_operators
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `<<` and `>>` shift operators.

methods.name: supports_boolean_literals
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports boolean literals (`true` and `false`). For example, in MSSQL these are treated as identifiers rather than boolean literals.

methods.name: supports_column_definition_trailing_commas
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports trailing commas in the column definitions list of a `CREATE` statement. Example: `CREATE TABLE T (x INT, y TEXT,)`

methods.name: supports_comma_separated_drop_column_list
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `ALTER TABLE tbl DROP COLUMN c1, ..., cn`

methods.name: supports_comma_separated_set_assignments
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports multiple `SET` statements in a single statement.

methods.name: supports_comma_separated_trim
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the two-argument comma-separated form of the `TRIM` function: `TRIM(expr, characters)`.

methods.name: supports_comment_on
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `COMMENT` statement

methods.name: supports_comment_optimizer_hint
methods.summary: Returns `true` if the dialect supports query optimizer hints in the format of single and multi line comments immediately following a `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `REPLACE`, `DELETE`, or `MERGE` keyword.

methods.name: supports_connect_by
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports CONNECT BY.

methods.name: supports_constraint_keyword_without_name
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `CONSTRAINT` keyword without a name in table constraint definitions.

methods.name: supports_create_index_with_clause
methods.summary: Does the dialect support with clause in create index statement? e.g. `CREATE INDEX idx ON t WITH (key = value, key2)`

methods.name: supports_create_table_like_parenthesized
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports specifying which table to copy the schema from inside parenthesis.

methods.name: supports_create_table_multi_schema_info_sources
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports specifying multiple options in a `CREATE TABLE` statement for the structure of the new table. For example: `CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT) AS SELECT 1 AS b, 2 AS a`

methods.name: supports_create_table_select
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `CREATE TABLE SELECT` statement

methods.name: supports_create_table_using
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `USING <format>` in `CREATE TABLE`.

methods.name: supports_create_view_comment_syntax
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `COMMENT` clause in `CREATE VIEW` statements using the `COMMENT = 'comment'` syntax.

methods.name: supports_cross_join_constraint
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports a join specification on CROSS JOIN.

methods.name: supports_cte_without_as
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `AS` keyword being optional in a CTE definition. For example: ```sql WITH cte_name (SELECT ...) ```

methods.name: supports_data_type_signed_suffix
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect allows an optional `SIGNED` suffix after integer data types.

methods.name: supports_detach
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `DETACH` statement.

methods.name: supports_dictionary_syntax
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports defining structs or objects using a syntax like `{'x': 1, 'y': 2, 'z': 3}`.

methods.name: supports_dollar_as_money_prefix
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports `$` as a prefix for money literals e.g. `SELECT $123.45` (SQL Server)

methods.name: supports_dollar_placeholder
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect allows dollar placeholders e.g. `SELECT $var` (SQLite)

methods.name: supports_double_ampersand_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect considers the `&&` operator as a boolean AND operator.

methods.name: supports_empty_projections
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports empty projections in SELECT statements

methods.name: supports_end_transaction_modifier
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `END {TRY | CATCH}` statements

methods.name: supports_eq_alias_assignment
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports treating the equals operator `=` within a `SelectItem` as an alias assignment operator, rather than a boolean expression. For example: the following statements are equivalent for such a dialect: ```sql…

methods.name: supports_execute_immediate
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` statements.

methods.name: supports_explain_with_utility_options
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `EXPLAIN` statements with utility options e.g. `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE TRUE, BUFFERS TRUE) SELECT * FROM tbl;`

methods.name: supports_extract_comma_syntax
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `EXTRACT` function with a comma separator instead of `FROM`.

methods.name: supports_factorial_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `a!` expressions

methods.name: supports_filter_during_aggregation
methods.summary: Does the dialect support `FILTER (WHERE expr)` for aggregate queries?

methods.name: supports_from_first_insert
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports "FROM-first" inserts.

methods.name: supports_from_first_select
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports "FROM-first" selects.

methods.name: supports_from_trailing_commas
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports trailing commas in the `FROM` clause of a `SELECT` statement. Example: `SELECT 1 FROM T, U, LIMIT 1`

methods.name: supports_geometric_types
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports geometric types.

methods.name: supports_group_by_expr
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialects supports `group sets, roll up, or cube` expressions.

methods.name: supports_group_by_with_modifier
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialects supports `GROUP BY` modifiers prefixed by a `WITH` keyword. Example: `GROUP BY value WITH ROLLUP`.

methods.name: supports_in_empty_list
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `(NOT) IN ()` expressions

methods.name: supports_insert_format
methods.summary: Does the dialect support insert formats, e.g. `INSERT INTO ... FORMAT <format>`

methods.name: supports_insert_set
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `INSERT INTO ... SET col1 = 1, ...` syntax.

methods.name: supports_insert_table_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports `INSERT INTO t [[AS] alias] ...`.

methods.name: supports_insert_table_function
methods.summary: Does the dialect support table function in insertion?

methods.name: supports_insert_table_query
methods.summary: Does the dialect support table queries in insertion?

methods.name: supports_install
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `INSTALL` statement.

methods.name: supports_interpolate
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `INTERPOLATE` clause in `ORDER BY` expressions.

methods.name: supports_interval_options
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `INTERVAL` data type with [Postgres]-style options.

methods.name: supports_key_column_option
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `KEY` keyword as part of column-level constraints in a `CREATE TABLE` statement.

methods.name: supports_lambda_functions
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports lambda functions, for example:

methods.name: supports_left_associative_joins_without_parens
methods.summary: Indicates whether the dialect supports left-associative join parsing by default when parentheses are omitted in nested joins.

methods.name: supports_limit_by
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `LIMIT BY` clause.

methods.name: supports_limit_comma
methods.summary: Does the dialect support parsing `LIMIT 1, 2` as `LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1`?

methods.name: supports_listen_notify
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `LISTEN`, `UNLISTEN` and `NOTIFY` statements

methods.name: supports_load_data
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `LOAD DATA` statement

methods.name: supports_load_extension
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `LOAD extension` statement

methods.name: supports_long_type_as_bigint
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect treats `LONG` as an alias for `BIGINT`.

methods.name: supports_map_literal_with_angle_brackets
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `MAP<K, V>` angle-bracket syntax for the MAP data type.

methods.name: supports_match_against
methods.summary: Does the dialect support the `MATCH() AGAINST()` syntax?

methods.name: supports_match_recognize
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the MATCH_RECOGNIZE operation.

methods.name: supports_multiline_comment_hints
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports optimizer hints in multiline comments e.g. `/*!50110 KEY_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024*/`

methods.name: supports_named_fn_args_with_assignment_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports named arguments of the form `FUN(a := '1', b := '2')`.

methods.name: supports_named_fn_args_with_colon_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports named arguments of the form `FUN(a : '1', b : '2')`.

methods.name: supports_named_fn_args_with_eq_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports named arguments of the form `FUN(a = '1', b = '2')`.

methods.name: supports_named_fn_args_with_expr_name
methods.summary: Returns true if dialect supports argument name as arbitrary expression. e.g. `FUN(LOWER('a'):'1',  b:'2')` Such function arguments are represented in the AST by the `FunctionArg::ExprNamed` variant, otherwise use the `FunctionArg::Named` v…

methods.name: supports_named_fn_args_with_rarrow_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports named arguments of the form `FUN(a => '1', b => '2')`.

methods.name: supports_nested_comments
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports nested comments e.g. `/* /* nested */ */`

methods.name: supports_notnull_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `x NOTNULL` operator expression.

methods.name: supports_numeric_literal_underscores
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports numbers containing underscores, e.g. `10_000_000`

methods.name: supports_numeric_prefix
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports identifiers starting with a numeric prefix such as tables named `59901_user_login`

methods.name: supports_object_name_double_dot_notation
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports double dot notation for object names

methods.name: supports_optimize_table
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `OPTIMIZE TABLE` statement.

methods.name: supports_order_by_all
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `ORDER BY ALL`. `ALL` which means all columns of the SELECT clause.

methods.name: supports_outer_join_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the `(+)` syntax for OUTER JOIN.

methods.name: supports_parens_around_table_factor
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports extra parentheses around lone table names or derived tables in the `FROM` clause.

methods.name: supports_parenthesized_set_variables
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports multiple variable assignment using parentheses in a `SET` variable declaration.

methods.name: supports_partiql
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports PartiQL for querying semi-structured data <https://partiql.org/index.html>

methods.name: supports_partition_by_after_order_by
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `PARTITION BY` appearing after `ORDER BY` in a `CREATE TABLE` statement (in addition to the standard placement before `ORDER BY`).

methods.name: supports_pipe_operator
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports pipe operator.

methods.name: supports_prewhere
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `PREWHERE` clause in `SELECT` statements.

methods.name: supports_projection_trailing_commas
methods.summary: Does the dialect support trailing commas in the projection list?

methods.name: supports_quote_delimited_string
methods.summary: Support quote delimited string literals, e.g. `Q'{...}'`

methods.name: supports_select_exclude
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports an exclude option as the last item in the projection section, not necessarily after a wildcard. For example: `SELECT *, c1, c2 EXCLUDE c3 FROM tbl`

methods.name: supports_select_expr_star
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports wildcard expansion on arbitrary expressions in projections.

methods.name: supports_select_format
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `FORMAT` clause in `SELECT` statements.

methods.name: supports_select_item_multi_column_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports parenthesized multi-column aliases in SELECT items. For example: ```sql SELECT stack(2, 'a', 'b') AS (col1, col2) ```

methods.name: supports_select_modifiers
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports MySQL-specific SELECT modifiers like `HIGH_PRIORITY`, `STRAIGHT_JOIN`, `SQL_SMALL_RESULT`, etc.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_except
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports an `EXCEPT` clause following a wildcard in a select list.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_exclude
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports an exclude option following a wildcard in the projection section. For example: `SELECT * EXCLUDE col1 FROM tbl`.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_ilike
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `ILIKE` option in a `SELECT *` wildcard expression.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_rename
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `RENAME` option in a `SELECT *` wildcard expression.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_replace
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `REPLACE` option in a `SELECT *` wildcard expression.

methods.name: supports_select_wildcard_with_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports aliasing a wildcard select item.

methods.name: supports_semantic_view_table_factor
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `SEMANTIC_VIEW()` table functions.

methods.name: supports_set_names
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `SET NAMES <charset_name> [COLLATE <collation_name>]`.

methods.name: supports_set_stmt_without_operator
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports `SET` statements without an explicit assignment operator such as `=`. For example: `SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON`.

methods.name: supports_settings
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `SETTINGS` clause.

methods.name: supports_show_like_before_in
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `LIKE 'pattern'` option in a `SHOW` statement before the `IN` option

methods.name: supports_space_separated_column_options
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports space-separated column options in a `CREATE TABLE` statement. For example: ```sql CREATE TABLE tbl (     col INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 ); ```

methods.name: supports_start_transaction_modifier
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `BEGIN {DEFERRED | IMMEDIATE | EXCLUSIVE | TRY | CATCH} [TRANSACTION]` statements

methods.name: supports_string_escape_constant
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the E'...' syntax for string literals

methods.name: supports_string_literal_backslash_escape
methods.summary: Determine if the dialect supports escaping characters via '\' in string literals.

methods.name: supports_string_literal_concatenation
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports concatenating of string literal Example: `SELECT 'Hello ' "world" => SELECT 'Hello world'`

methods.name: supports_string_literal_concatenation_with_newline
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports concatenating string literals with a newline. For example, the following statement would return `true`: ```sql SELECT 'abc' in (   'a'   'b'   'c' ); ```

methods.name: supports_struct_literal
methods.summary: Return true if the dialect supports the STRUCT literal

methods.name: supports_subquery_as_function_arg
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports a subquery passed to a function as the only argument without enclosing parentheses.

methods.name: supports_table_hints
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports the table hints in the `FROM` clause.

methods.name: supports_table_sample_before_alias
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `TABLESAMPLE` option before the table alias option. For example:

methods.name: supports_table_versioning
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports querying historical table data by specifying which version of the data to query.

methods.name: supports_top_before_distinct
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect expects the `TOP` option before the `ALL`/`DISTINCT` options in a `SELECT` statement.

methods.name: supports_trailing_commas
methods.summary: Does the dialect support trailing commas around the query?

methods.name: supports_triple_quoted_string
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports triple quoted string e.g. `"""abc"""`

methods.name: supports_try_convert
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `TRY_CONVERT` function

methods.name: supports_unicode_string_literal
methods.summary: Determine if the dialect supports string literals with `U&` prefix. This is used to specify Unicode code points in string literals. For example, in PostgreSQL, the following is a valid string literal: ```sql SELECT U&'\0061\0062\0063'; ```…

methods.name: supports_update_order_by
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `ORDER BY` in `UPDATE` statements.

methods.name: supports_user_host_grantee
methods.summary: Does the dialect support MySQL-style `'user'@'host'` grantee syntax?

methods.name: supports_values_as_table_factor
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports `VALUES` as a table factor without requiring parentheses around the entire clause.

methods.name: supports_window_clause_named_window_reference
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports referencing another named window within a window clause declaration.

methods.name: supports_window_function_null_treatment_arg
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialects supports specifying null treatment as part of a window function's parameter list as opposed to after the parameter list.

methods.name: supports_with_fill
methods.summary: Returns true if this dialect supports the `WITH FILL` clause in `ORDER BY` expressions.

methods.name: supports_within_after_array_aggregation
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports `ARRAY_AGG() [WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY)]` expressions. Otherwise, the dialect should expect an `ORDER BY` without the `WITHIN GROUP` clause, e.g. [`ANSI`]

methods.name: supports_xml_expressions
methods.summary: Returns true if the dialect supports XML-related expressions such as `xml '<foo/>'` typed strings, XML functions like `XMLCONCAT`, `XMLELEMENT`, etc.
